audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.75%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.10%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.26%, mentre il VIX è salito dello 0.95%. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4800 dollari l'oncia, con un rialzo dello 0.51%. Il petrolio è sceso del 3.28%, mentre il Dollar Index è calato dello 0.11%.

La situazione in Medio Oriente resta tesa, con notizie di un possibile aumento della produzione petrolifera negli USA e un aumento della domanda di petrolio crudo statunitense.

In agenda oggi, nessun dato macroeconomico rilevante. La BCE ha pubblicato i verbali della riunione, suggerendo che il consiglio direttivo potrebbe aver bisogno di ulteriori prove prima di aumentare i tassi.

Ethereum e BNB hanno variazioni più moderate, con Ethereum in crescita dello zero virgola trentanove percento a due mille trecentoquarantatré dollari e BNB in aumento dell'uno virgola quarantadue percento a seicentoventinove virgola sessantaquattro dollari.", 'sentiment': 'Il Fear & Greed Index è a 21, in territorio di Extreme Fear.'}

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'evoluzione dei mercati europei e americani, con particolare attenzione agli indici PMI e ai dati sull'inflazione. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 
In Asian markets, the Nikkei closed at 58,476, down 1.75%, while the Shanghai index ended at 4051.43, down 0.10%. 
These moves suggest a cautious start for European and US markets.

In Western markets, the S&P 500 rose 0.26%, while the VIX increased 0.95%. 
The Dollar Index dropped 0.11%, and gold holds above $4800/oz with a 0.51% gain. 
Oil prices declined, with Brent down 3.28% to $96.13. 

On the macro front, ECB minutes suggest the governing council may need more evidence before making significant policy changes. 
China's growth hit 5% despite global tensions. 
The US and Europe are monitoring the Iran situation, which is impacting crude oil supply and prices.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is up one point one four percent, trading above seventy-five thousand dollars. The ETF daily net inflow is twenty-six point one million dollars. 

In the altcoin space, Ethereum is up zero point three nine percent to two thousand three hundred forty-three dollars. Solana is up three point zero one percent to eighty-seven point seven three dollars. Binance Coin is up one point four two percent to six hundred twenty-nine point six four dollars.

The Fear & Greed Index is at twenty-one, indicating Extreme Fear.

Thanks for tuning in. Keep an eye on market trends for tomorrow and we'll be back with more updates. Until then, goodbye and good luck with your trades. Have a great day!

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. Has the ECB’s rationale for the digital euro evolved over time, from a response to tech…

articles.title: Winning in the Donbas: What Russia’s 2014–2015 Campaign Reveals About Modern War
articles.snippet: It is clear that the U.S.-Israeli decapitation, airpower-centric, and precision strike campaign are again not enough to bring about the two countries’ strategic goals. The United States still finds itself potentially having to commit land forces into its war with Iran, yet many unknowns lurk, including a fragile ceasefire and a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: What’s Next for Oil Prices?
articles.snippet: Oil prices have held steady below $100 per barrel since the U.S. on Monday initiated a naval blockade to deter Iran-linked ships from passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The three days of calmer oil futures markets so far this week aren’t expected to last long amid the volatile geopolitical situation at the world’s most vital oil shipping lane. The price of oil has the potential to either surge to new highs or slump to pre-war levels, depending on the U.S.-Iran talks, but most of all—on the status of navigability of the Strait…
